items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: She said, 'Well, I don't understand this. He wouldn't have done that for Chet Baker.'

ctx.x: It was a small car. It looked like an economy car, you know. But anyway, he drove straight through to St. Louis. In the meanwhile he and his wife were going through divorce procedures, and he had an apartment on 59th Street, just across the street from the -- what was the name of that club? [Premier] I think was the name of it. It was run by -- I can't think of his name. Anyway, he had this apartment on 59th Street. So she had to fly down to St. Louis to get some

papers signed and he found out I was in jail, and they didn't write any narcotic bails at that time, you know. So he sent back $2,500.00 cash by her to bail me out of jail. She said, 'Well, I don't understand this. He wouldn't have done that for Chet Baker.' You know. 'And he's doing this for you, you know.' And at that year I had just turned 40. I said, 'Well, life begins at 40.' You know. So here I am. So she had me over to the apartment that night, and they had just had their first child, a son. They named him…
